article_title: Pathways to Learning: Exploring High School Students' Learning of AI-Powered Educational Robotics
citation: G. McLaughlin, E. Novak, S. Ahmadi, J. Li, Y. Guo, R. Liu, & L. Borgerding. (2026). Pathways to learning: exploring high school students' learning of AI-powered educational robotics. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-026-10651-w
title: Project-based robotics + AI curriculum structured by P3 Task Taxonomy with backward design
description: The curriculum comprised 10 lessons followed by a robotics engineering design challenge, aligned with K-12 CS standards and structured using Barak and Assal's P3 Task Taxonomy: Practice tasks with predefined solutions, Problem Solving tasks allowing multiple approaches, and Project tasks as complex student-driven endeavors. It was developed with backward design, starting from the design challenge and working backward to essential learning objectives.
requirements: mBot robotics kits with the mBlock block-based coding platform including AI/ML extensions
constraints: Sensor-based programming relied on student-written rules rather than data-driven learning, serving as a conceptual foundation for AI
examples: Lesson 8 had students train an image recognition model by collecting datasets, labeling images, and iteratively evaluating model performance
key_sources: G. McLaughlin, E. Novak, S. Ahmadi, J. Li, Y. Guo, R. Liu, & L. Borgerding. (2026). Pathways to learning: exploring high school students' learning of AI-powered educational robotics. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-026-10651-w

article_title: Less Efficient Neural Processing Related to Irregular Sleep and Less Sustained Attention in Toddlers
citation: Hoyniak, C. P., Petersen, I. T., McQuillan, M. E., Staples, A. D., & Bates, J. E. (2015). Less Efficient Neural Processing Related to Irregular Sleep and Less Sustained Attention in Toddlers. Developmental Neuropsychology. https://doi.org/10.1080/87565641.2015.1016162
title: P3 latency as an index of neural efficiency of attentional processing in early childhood
description: This framework holds that the P3 ERP component elicited by target stimuli in Oddball tasks indexes attentional and information processing capacity, with "larger amplitudes and shorter latencies... generally associated with better attentional and information processing capacity." Longer P3 latencies indicate poorer neural efficiency surrounding attentional processes. The article applies this framework to toddlers, using target P3 latency as a neurophysiological index linking irregular sleep to sustained attention capacity.
requirements: ERP recording during an active Oddball task with identifiable target P3 component, typically via parietal electrode clusters identified through spatial PCA
constraints: The article notes the P3 is an index of multiple cognitive processes with multiple neural generators, so few specific interpretations have been consistently supported; in toddlers it is uncertain whether the elicited component reflects the same P3 as in adults
examples: The study elicited a P3-like component from toddlers during an active auditory Oddball task and found longer latencies associated with poorer sustained attention and more irregular sleep
key_sources: Hoyniak, C. P., Petersen, I. T., McQuillan, M. E., Staples, A. D., & Bates, J. E. (2015). Less Efficient Neural Processing Related to Irregular Sleep and Less Sustained Attention in Toddlers. Developmental Neuropsychology. https://doi.org/10.1080/87565641.2015.1016162

article_title: Changes in attentional resources during the acquisition of laparoscopic surgical skills.
citation: Thomaschewski M, Heldmann M, Uter J C, Varbelow D, Münte T F, Keck T. (2021). Changes in attentional resources during the acquisition of laparoscopic surgical skills. BJS Open. https://doi.org/10.1093/bjsopen/zraa012
title: P300 amplitude as an index of mental resource allocation in dual-task situations
description: The framework treats the P300 component of the event-related brain potential to stimuli in a secondary task as a marker of how many mental resources remain for that task while a primary task is performed. As the article states, "The amplitude of the P300 component has been interpreted as an index for mental resources that are available for processing of the task at hand, with reduced P300 indicating reduced mental resources". Reduced P300 to secondary-task targets after training therefore indicates fewer resources allotted to the secondary task and, by inference, more available for the primary surgical motor task.
requirements: A dual-task paradigm with a defined secondary stimulus stream and EEG recording
constraints: The present evidence covers novice learners in early training stages only
target_learning_goals: tracking mental resource allocation during surgical skill acquisition
examples: EEG recorded before and after a 5-week LTB curriculum while participants performed the pack-your-luggage exercise with a concurrent auditory change detection task
key_sources: Thomaschewski M, Heldmann M, Uter J C, Varbelow D, Münte T F, Keck T. (2021). Changes in attentional resources during the acquisition of laparoscopic surgical skills. BJS Open. https://doi.org/10.1093/bjsopen/zraa012

article_title: A Case Study: Novel Group Interactions through Introductory Computational Physics
citation: Michael J. Obsniuk, Paul W. Irving, and Marcos D. Caballero. (2015). A Case Study: Novel Group Interactions through Introductory Computational Physics. https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.05457
title: Projects and Practices in Physics (P3): a restructured introductory calculus-based mechanics course with group VPython modeling projects
description: P3 is a newly adopted format of introductory calculus-based mechanics at Michigan State University in which "groups of students work on short modeling projects – which make use of a novel inquiry-based approach – to develop their understanding of both physics content and practice." It builds on the Matter & Interactions curriculum with a computational element using VPython. Students negotiate meaning in small groups, develop a shared vision for their group's approach, and employ science practices to navigate complex physics problems, with computers treated as indispensable modern tools that students must generate meaningful direction for.
requirements: Groups of students must leverage their understanding of fundamental physical principles to model real world phenomena computationally, i.e. generate meaningful direction to a computer, since computers do not generate meaningful direction on their own.
target_learners: introductory calculus-based mechanics undergraduates at Michigan State University
examples: The case-study group's fourth-week project required creating a computational model to simulate the geostationary orbit of a satellite around Earth, incorporating a position dependent Newtonian gravitational force and the update of momentum using realistic numerical values.
key_sources: Michael J. Obsniuk, Paul W. Irving, and Marcos D. Caballero. (2015). A Case Study: Novel Group Interactions through Introductory Computational Physics. https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.05457

article_title: ${\rm P}^3$: A Practice Focused Learning Environment
citation: Paul W. Irving, Michael J. Obsniuk, and Marcos D. Caballero. (2016). P3: A Practice Focused Learning Environment. https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.04455
title: P3 (Projects and Practices in Physics) introductory mechanics course
description: P3 is a transformed, introductory, calculus-based mechanics course for science and engineering majors grounded in evidence-based pedagogy and built on Matter & Interactions. The article states "students will solve one of these complex, real-world problems in each two-hour class meeting (twice per week)", with roughly 30 such problems across the semester, 7 of them computational modeling problems. Students negotiate approaches in groups of 4 with minimally facilitated discussion, present solutions to tutors, and the course is organized around conservation of momentum, energy, and angular momentum.
requirements: Instructional staff positioned as facilitators; groups of 4 with minimally facilitated discussion; tutors probe solutions with tutoring questions.
constraints: The article states full adoption "might be challenging in diﬀerent contexts" and that the separation of lecture and lab at MSU meant students could not work with laboratory equipment in lecture.
target_learners: science and engineering majors in introductory calculus-based mechanics
examples: The Escape from Ice Station McMurdo project has students model hovercraft motion analytically from position-time data, then computationally with air drag, culminating in an accident-report simulation.
key_sources: Paul W. Irving, Michael J. Obsniuk, and Marcos D. Caballero. (2016). P3: A Practice Focused Learning Environment. https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.04455

article_title: ${\rm P}^3$: A Practice Focused Learning Environment
citation: Paul W. Irving, Michael J. Obsniuk, and Marcos D. Caballero. (2016). P3: A Practice Focused Learning Environment. https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.04455
title: P3 modeling framework (PCubED): real world, model world, outcomes, validation cycle
description: The Modeling Framework (Fig. 1) organizes student engagement: students "begin their work by considering a Real World situation", create a Model World in which they explicitly articulate assumptions and approximations while designing the system and generating representations, use graphs, equations, and diagrams to predict Outcomes, and validate those Outcomes against real-world results, data, or expectations. The article stresses that students develop "a solution to the problem, not simply ﬁnding an answer", with the whole modeling process discussed with course staff once students feel they have sufficiently completed a problem.
requirements: A complex, real-world problem statement to start from; group negotiation of assumptions and approximations; representations (graphs, equations, diagrams) for prediction; real-world results or expectations for validation.
constraints: Developed considering the contextual limitation that MSU lecture sections are divorced from laboratory equipment, so modeling uses analytical and computational solutions rather than experiments.
target_learners: introductory calculus-based mechanics students in groups of 4
examples: In the hovercraft project, students model motion from position vs time data, predict when hovercrafts meet, and validate predictions against given outcomes.
key_sources: Paul W. Irving, Michael J. Obsniuk, and Marcos D. Caballero. (2016). P3: A Practice Focused Learning Environment. https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.04455

article_title: Teaching Computation in Introductory Physics using Complex Problems
citation: Marcos D. Caballero, Michael J. Obsniuk, Paul W. Irving. (2017). Teaching Computation in Introductory Physics using Complex Problems. https://pcubed.pa.msu.edu
title: Projects and Practices in Physics (P3): a group-based introductory mechanics course integrating computation without a coupled laboratory
description: P3 is an introductory mechanics course at Michigan State University where students work in groups of four on open-ended, context-rich problems called projects, using analytical and computational techniques. It was developed for a setting where lecture and laboratory are decoupled, reducing class size to about 100 students, and is structured around the Matter and Interactions textbook while emphasizing the three conservation principles of mechanics. The course uses a flipped model with pre-class readings, videos, and homework, and its materials are available online at pcubed.pa.msu.edu.
requirements: Pre-class readings, lecture videos, and homework that prime students for in-class group problem solving
Tutors who give formative feedback on problem-solving approach and group work
constraints: Designed for a context where lecture and laboratory courses are divorced, so it does not rely on laboratory course coupling
target_learners: calculus-based introductory mechanics students in science and engineering
examples: Students solve a hovercraft rescue project analytically in one class period, then extend it computationally with air resistance the next
key_sources: Marcos D. Caballero, Michael J. Obsniuk, Paul W. Irving. (2017). Teaching Computation in Introductory Physics using Complex Problems. https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.05493

article_title: Teaching Computation in Introductory Physics using Complex Problems
citation: Marcos D. Caballero, Michael J. Obsniuk, Paul W. Irving. (2017). Teaching Computation in Introductory Physics using Complex Problems. https://pcubed.pa.msu.edu
title: Sequence of seven computational projects across the semester building from constant velocity to multi-principle models
description: P3 embeds computational modeling in seven of its fourteen semester projects, sequenced to grow in complexity: modeling relative and constant velocity, constant force motion with air resistance, gravitationally interacting bodies in orbit, energy of a gravitational system, collisions with an if-statement detection, rotation of an extended body, and a final defense-system project using all three conservation principles. Projects and supporting materials are available online at pcubed.pa.msu.edu. The sequence moves students from writing loops and producing graphs to adding control structures and rotational models.
requirements: Minimal working programs and pre-class homework supporting each project
constraints: Computational modeling appears in 7 of 14 total projects, not every project
target_learners: introductory mechanics students in science and engineering
target_learning_goals: iterative motion prediction with Euler-Cromer step
conservation of momentum, energy, and angular momentum
constructing integration loops and control structures
examples: Project 11 has students develop an if statement to detect a collision and apply conservation of linear momentum to determine post-collision velocities
key_sources: Marcos D. Caballero, Michael J. Obsniuk, Paul W. Irving. (2017). Teaching Computation in Introductory Physics using Complex Problems. https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.05493
